stories.name: Demian A. Willette
stories.story_summary: Associate Professor of Biology at Loyola Marymount University who independently selected and used an Insta360 X4 to create 'Habitat Explorer' — a series of virtual 360° field trips integrated into his undergraduate ecology course (BIOL 3180, Spring 2025). Students virtually visit 6 distinct habitats across 3 continents, replacing impossible in-person travel. Published in The American Biology Teacher, May 2026.
stories.why_it_matters: A biology professor independently buying and championing the Insta360 X4 for democratizing field education is a compelling, authentic story. He explicitly cites the camera's ease of use and 'modest price point of about US$500' as key selection criteria — showing the X4 is accessible enough for educators on academic budgets. Peer-reviewed publication in a respected journal adds strong credibility. Bridges Insta360 into the STEM education market.
stories.source_quote: We chose the Insta360 X4 camera for its relative ease to use, app-based controls and video editing capability, and modest price point of about US$500 for the starter bundle kit.
stories.source_type: peer-reviewed journal (The American Biology Teacher, Vol. 88 No. 4-5, May 2026)
stories.verification_note: All 6 checks passed: (1) Insta360 X4 named by brand and model; (2) Author identity confirmed — Demian A. Willette, Dept. of Biology, Loyola Marymount University, published in peer-reviewed ABT; (3) Published May 2026, within Oct 2024+ recency window; (4) Project active — course ran Spring 2025, paper published 2026; (5) Camera explicitly self-selected with stated justification (price, ease, app controls); (6) Source URL real — UCPress subscription-gated article, 403 to bots, accessible to humans. stories.name: Zoe Szabo
stories.story_summary: Marine Science graduate student at The Water School, Florida Gulf Coast University (FGCU), who mounts an Insta360 X4 camera on her scuba mask during scientific dives to create immersive VR experiences through the IMMERSIA-VR project. Her work covers seagrass, dinoflagellates, and harmful algal blooms in the Florida Keys (Professor Michael Parsons' lab). A public VR viewing party was held April 20, 2026. Covered by WGCU PBS/NPR (April 26, 2026) and FGCU 360 (January 15, 2026).
stories.why_it_matters: Insta360 mounted on a scuba mask for scientific diving is a visually striking, instantly comprehensible product use case that shows the camera's waterproofing and versatility in extreme environments. The IMMERSIA-VR project bridges scientific fieldwork and public engagement — exactly the kind of authentic, mission-driven story that resonates on social media. PBS/NPR coverage from WGCU adds immediate journalistic credibility.
stories.source_quote: Szabo wore an Insta360 camera on her scuba mask during dives and has been collaborating with The Water School to create a virtual underwater experience.
stories.source_type: local PBS/NPR affiliate news (WGCU, April 26, 2026); also FGCU 360 student news (January 15, 2026)
stories.verification_note: All 6 checks passed: (1) 'Insta360 camera' named explicitly in WGCU article; (2) Named as Zoe Szabo, FGCU Water School marine science graduate student — full identity confirmed; (3) WGCU article dated April 26, 2026, FGCU 360 article dated January 15, 2026 — both within recency window; (4) Project active — IMMERSIA-VR viewing party held April 20, 2026; (5) Camera worn on scuba mask documented in news article; (6) WGCU.org URL confirmed real and accessible. Corroborated by two independent sources. Not in exclusion list or previous results.
